Subject: On‑prem observability handoff & SIEM ingestion details (Cygnus)

Marcel —

Thanks for taking the time last week. As discussed, we want to confirm the observability handoff requirements for your on‑prem deployment (VPC + enclave) so our private agent/forwarder can be provisioned without surprises. Below is a concise checklist and a couple of follow ups we need from your side before the Handoff meeting on Tuesday.

Primary goals:
- Deliver logs, metrics, and tracing in a way that meets Cygnus security controls (mTLS + limited egress)
- Ensure SIEM (Splunk/HEC) ingestion meets schema and retention expectations
- Provide clear tracing hooks (OTel spans + ID propagation) for request correlation into Cygnus APM

Network / connectivity notes (summary):
- Outbound egress only to 35.154.22.11:443 (Redwood forwarder ingress) — IP allowlist preferred; fallback: FQDN with cert pinning
- mTLS required between on‑prem forwarder and Redwood collector (client certs managed by Cygnus PKI or Redwood-issued short‑lived certs via ACME integration)
- TCP 514 (syslog) allowed internally to forwarder; forwarder will translate to HTTPS/HEC for Cygnus SIEM as requested
- Tracing: OTLP/gRPC on 4317 internally, forwarded as OTLP/HTTP where necessary. We will preserve trace.parent/trace.id across hops.

SIEM specifics we need from you:
1) HEC endpoint(s) (ip:port or FQDN), token format, and expected index names
2) Expected retention window for observability data (logs/metrics/traces) — default Redwood retention for private is 30 days unless otherwise negotiated
3) Any mandatory field mappings or enrichment rules (e.g., asset_id, tenant_id, product_tag) you expect before indexing

Attachments: I attached a short sample config we use as a starting point (onprem-obsv-sample-config.yaml) and the evidence export spec we discussed (cygnus-evidence-export-spec.pdf). Please review section 2.1 (HEC mapping) and 3.2 (trace tagging).

Proposed next steps / asks for Cygnus before the handshake call:
- Marcel: confirm HEC URL + token format and whether you require TLS client certs for HEC
- Security tooling team: anything special about syslog headers or CEF formatting we should preserve?
- Cygnus ops: confirm allowed egress model (IP allowlist vs FQDN) and preferred keying for tenant scoping

We will schedule the 60‑minute Handoff (technical meetup) for Tue 11/23 09:00 PT, tentative invite attached. Karthik and Kimberly will lead the config review.

Thanks —

Priya —

Thanks for the clear checklist. A few quick answers while I validate specifics with our SIEM ops team:

1) HEC endpoint: https://hec.cygnus.internal:8088 — we use token-based auth. Token format is a 128‑bit hex string that we will provide via secure vault; we require TLS server cert pinning for external forwarders.
2) Retention: Logs 90 days, metrics 180 days, traces 30 days (these are the default for our compliance profile; we can negotiate a trimmed retention window for Redwood copies if needed)
3) Field mappings: We require asset_id (UUID v4), service_name, environment, and request_id fields present on every log/event. If Redwood is enriching, please use "asset_id" and "tenant_id" as primary keys.

Notes on connectivity:
- We prefer IP allowlist for the forwarder; I will propose two stable egress IPs from our net team.
- We will issue client certs from our internal PKI for mTLS to Redwood (we need instructions for CSR template).
- For tracing, Pauline asked whether Redwood can preserve OpenTelemetry baggage across async job queues — she flagged that our distributed tracing relies on trace_id propagation through our job broker.

I will confirm the token exchange process and share the cert CSR template by EOD tomorrow.

— Marcel
Marcel D'Souza
Lead, Security Tooling — Cygnus Systems

Marcel —

Appreciate the quick responses. A couple of implementation notes / clarifications from engineering side: we attached a minimal CSR template in the sample config and a recommended OTLP/HTTP fallback snippet. Key points:

- CSR: please include subjectAltName with the forwarder FQDN and include the organizationalUnitName set to "Cygnus-Observability". If you prefer Redwood to generate the cert and rotate it, we can support short‑lived cert rotation via ACME (requires inbound reachability to a small provisioning endpoint).

- HEC: Redwood forwarder will send to your HEC over HTTPS with token in Authorization header. We can optionally add an HEC envelope attribute for asset_id/enrichment prior to indexing. Example header: Authorization: Splunk <token>

- Field mapping: we will map local fields to your required keys. Example JSON event we send: {"timestamp":"...","asset_id":"<uuid>","service_name":"redwood-forwarder","environment":"prod","request_id":"<x>"} — we will keep the original raw message in a "raw_event" field to preserve fidelity for audits.

- Tracing: we will preserve trace_id and parent_span_id. For the job broker case, we recommend instrumenting the job producer/consumer to propagate the W3C traceparent header; Redwood will forward the header unchanged. For async systems where baggage isn't available, we can patch by emitting a linking event that references the originating request_id.

Action items for the Handoff call:
- Cygnus: share the CSR (or confirm ACME approach) and the HEC token exchange method
- Redwood: provide an HEC indexing sample and retention contract clause we can attach to the SOW (I'll follow up with a small draft)

I will be on the call and will share the collector runbook screen (sample config + routing rules).

Thanks —
Karthik
